status.en: 21 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 110% more than the week before, most of them in La Espriella, Espriella and Catatumbo.
status.nb: 21 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 110 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i La Espriella, Espriella og Catatumbo.

summary.en: Colombia opened an embassy in Jerusalem while UN independent experts urged Ecopetrol to provide reparations to armed-conflict victims and the UN Security Council heard calls for the peace deal to endure as insecurity grows. Opposition groups protested budget cuts that threaten the peace court and searches for the disappeared, and the peace tribunal charged former FARC members with anti-Indigenous crimes. Rebels detonated a car bomb outside a toll booth in Cauca, FARC dissidents were killed in a Catatumbo operation, and an army airstrike hit a teenager. 225 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Colombia åpnet en ambassade i Jerusalem mens FN-uavhengige eksperter oppfordret Ecopetrol til å yte erstatning til ofre for væpnet konflikt, og FN-sikkerhetsrådet hørte oppfordringer om at fredsavtalen skal holde i møte med økende usikkerhet. Opposisjonsgrupper protesterte mot budsjettkutt som truer fredsdomstolen og søk etter de forsvunne, og fredsretten anklaget tidligere FARC-medlemmer for anti-urfolks-forbrytelser. Rebeller detonerte en bilbombe utenfor en bomstasjon i Cauca, FARC-dissidenter ble drept i en operasjon i Catatumbo, og et luftangrep fra hæren traff en tenåring. 225 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
